abstract: Type IV pili are widespread bacterial nanomachines that mediate adhesion, motility and host interactions, yet the molecular mechanism coordinating assembly of their outer-membrane channel with attachment to the bacterial cell wall has remained unknown. Here, we show that the conserved PilQ-associated protein TsaP functions as a conformationally regulated envelope adaptor linking secretin assembly to cell-wall anchoring. A crystal structure of full-length TsaP, integrated with structural, biophysical and functional analyses, reveals a compact autoinhibited conformation in which the N-terminal LysM domain is sequestered against the protein core. Comparative structural analyses support a mechanism in which PilQ association remodels TsaP, exposing the LysM domain for peptidoglycan binding. Together, our findings support a mechanistic model in which PilQ-dependent conformational activation of TsaP couples secretin assembly to cell-wall anchoring, providing a framework for understanding the regulated integration of type IV pilus machineries within the bacterial envelope.
